title: Collaboration: Deduplicate and Order Retried Messages
businessContext: After reconnecting, a team chat shows duplicate messages and places delayed deliveries after newer messages.
problemStatement: Implement solution({ channelId, messages, incoming }). Existing messages are valid and have unique IDs/sequences in this channel. A message has nonempty string id/channelId, positive safe-integer seq, and string body. For each incoming record: invalid shape => invalid; foreign channel => forbidden; an existing ID with identical seq/body => duplicate, otherwise conflict; an occupied seq under another ID => conflict; otherwise accepted. Return { messages, outcomes }, ordered by ascending seq. Inputs are plain objects; incoming records may have missing or invalid fields.
constraints: Implement the synchronous solution(input) contract exactly. Do not mutate input; all inputs are JSON data.
This is a deterministic state model. It does not open sockets, send notifications, authorize real users, or establish media connections.
candidateTasks: Reproduce the starter failure, implement the invariant, and pass every authored case.
How would you persist server-assigned ordering and idempotency keys across concurrent message producers?
starterCode: function solution({messages, incoming}) { return {messages: messages.concat(incoming), outcomes: incoming.map(() => 'accepted')}; }

testCases.name: Deduplicate a retry in the same batch
Reject changed payload under same ID
Validate malformed and unsafe sequence fields

hints: Write down validation and replay precedence before changing state.
Use stable IDs and monotonic sequence/version values; preserve input ownership.
alternativeApproaches: Use an append-only event log with transactional projections.
Use a database snapshot plus a versioned resume cursor.
commonMistakes: Trusting delivery order or treating retries as new operations.
Mutating caller-owned arrays or accepting cross-channel data.
Presenting a fixture result as a guarantee of real-time delivery or media connectivity.
